wire.headline: Energy Firm Reports Revenue Rise Amid Profit Drop and Job Cuts
sentences: Revenue increased by 7% year-on-year to 4.26bn GBP for the quarter to 30 September.
The company's pre-tax profit declined by 12% to 310m GBP.
The firm announced plans to cut 850 jobs, representing about 6% of its workforce.
Two gas plants, one in Wales and one in Kent, are scheduled to close by March 2027.
CEO Marian Holt stated that cost pressure has been sharper than expected.
Ofgem has opened an investigation into the company's billing system.
The dividend was held at 12.4p a share.

PD.headline: Kestrel Securities Cuts 850 Jobs Amidst Rising Costs

ND.headline: Energy Firm Announces Job Cuts and Profit Drop Amid Regulatory Scrutiny

sentences.text: The company reported a pre-tax profit decline of 12% to 310m GBP.
Plans were revealed to cut 850 jobs, which represents about 6% of the workforce.
A Kestrel Securities analyst stated that these job cuts will save 90m GBP a year.
Negotiations with unions are set to begin on 4 November.
The union Unite intends to ballot members on taking industrial action.
The company stated that there will be no compulsory redundancies before January 2027.
Since 2024, 1,200 staff have left the company under a voluntary scheme.
The Kent plant, which employs 410 staff, has a local supply chain that is now exposed.
The MP for Deeside has requested an urgent meeting with the company.
A customer group logged 3,400 billing complaints in six months.
Ofgem fined the company 1.8m GBP in 2023 over billing issues.
Ofgem is scheduled to report preliminary findings by end of 2026.
Kestrel Securities reduced its price target to 240p from 290p.
